name: Failed-payment recovery add-on for tiny Stripe SaaS
buyer: Solo/indie SaaS founders on Stripe with <$20k MRR
pain: Involuntary churn from failed cards; founders do not measure recovery

evidence.shows: Payment recovery included on all plans; Starter $250/mo billed yearly ($300 monthly) (fact)
Smart Retries, overdue reminders and up to 3 recovery automations listed as Included; Billing 0.7% of volume pay-as-you-go (fact)
A solo founder's WorkAid Dunning (Stripe failed-payment visibility) listed at $0/mo revenue; founder says recovery is rarely measured (fact); shows crowding by other micro-entrants
Claims involuntary churn is 20-40% of churn and tooling recovers 40-80% (secondary blog claim, unverified)
Platform natively retries (default 8 tries in 2 weeks); hard-decline cards not retried; Stripe can change/expand native features at any time (fact)

entrant_wedge: Cheap dunning email/card-update-page for sub-$20k MRR Stripe shops

entrant_edge.entrant_basis: Entrant would charge ~$19/mo; but the native incumbent is $0, so entrant has NO cost edge
entrant_edge.falsifier: If >=30% of surveyed sub-$20k MRR Stripe founders say native Smart Retries leaves meaningful unrecovered revenue they would pay for, wedge survives; otherwise dead

unit_economics.notes: Model: $19/mo, email+hosting variable ~ $1; no evidence anyone pays

regulatory_or_platform_dependency: Depends on Stripe API/Connect OAuth; Stripe native features directly substitute
major_uncertainty: Free native Stripe feature already covers most of it; no entrant edge

dimension_reasons.demand_signal: Only one dated blog and a $0-revenue clone; no paying-behavior signal
dimension_reasons.acquisition_efficiency: No evidenced free channel; IH crowded
dimension_reasons.competition_gap: Stripe Smart Retries free + Churnkey + clones
dimension_reasons.regulatory_simplicity: Card data stays with Stripe; low regulation

verdict_reason: Native free incumbent (Stripe Smart Retries) and crowded clones; no unknown-entrant edge
unknowns: Actual recovery uplift of third-party vs native not verified
Third-party recovery rates are blog claims

name: Missed-call text-back for home-service trades

evidence.shows: Starter $97/mo, Unlimited $297/mo, Agency Pro $497/mo; page does not name missed-call text-back (fact)
Pricing not published, sales-gated; page does not mention missed-call text-back (fact)
SMS $0.0083/segment plus carrier fees $0.0035-0.005 outbound; 10DLC onboarding fees apply (fact)
10DLC brand $4-$44 one-time, campaign $15 one-time, $0.75-$10/mo; carriers block unregistered traffic; approval 2-4 weeks at time of writing (fact, dated 2023, fees may have changed)

entrant_edge.entrant_basis: Entrant faces same carrier registration (2-4 wks at 2023); no shortcut
entrant_edge.falsifier: If a pooled/ISV 10DLC registration lets customers send within 2 days at <$5 cost, edge would appear

unit_economics.notes: Model: ~100 texts/mo at ~$0.013 plus number rental; support unknown

regulatory_or_platform_dependency: Carrier/CTIA 10DLC and TCPA consent rules; Twilio or carriers can suspend
major_uncertainty: Per-customer brand registration and support burden; unknown demand

dimension_reasons.contribution_economics: Model 84% margin but registration/support cost uncounted
dimension_reasons.acquisition_efficiency: No channel evidence; unknown entrant, cold local trades
dimension_reasons.automation: Message flow automatable, onboarding/registration is manual
dimension_reasons.competition_gap: GHL, Podium, many resellers (price page not showing standalone)

verdict_reason: Compliance/registration friction and bundled incumbents; no evidence of demand or edge

name: State sales-tax nexus tracker for small SaaS/ecommerce sellers
buyer: Micro-SaaS founders selling in multiple US states
pain: Unaware when they cross economic-nexus thresholds

evidence.shows: Stripe Tax monitors registration thresholds (incl. VAT OSS) and alerts via dashboard/email (fact)
Stripe Tax listed at 0.5% per transaction in registered jurisdictions (third-party, unverified vs Stripe)
Typical nexus: $100K sales or 200 transactions; some states repealed transaction prong; 200-transaction test 'SaaS-hostile' (secondary blog)

entrant_wedge: Read-only threshold dashboard across payment processors

entrant_edge.entrant_basis: Stripe threshold monitoring has no separate listed fee; entrant would add cost
entrant_edge.falsifier: Founders not on Stripe or needing multi-processor view willing to pay; else no gap

regulatory_or_platform_dependency: State rules change; liability risk if advice is wrong; processor API access
major_uncertainty: Liability for wrong threshold data; Stripe already covers it

dimension_reasons.demand_signal: One secondary blog, no paying signal
dimension_reasons.competition_gap: Stripe Tax and others already alert

verdict_reason: Stripe already monitors thresholds; rule-maintenance liability; no edge
unknowns: State-by-state rule data source and cost unverified

name: Simple e-signature for small landlords/contractors

evidence.shows: Free 3 docs/mo; Light $10/mo yearly ($12 monthly); Business $30/mo yearly (fact)
ESIGN Act: signatures cannot be denied legal effect solely for being electronic; so low legal barrier (fact)

entrant_edge.entrant_basis: Incumbent free tier is $0; entrant cannot undercut
entrant_edge.falsifier: Landlords exceeding 3 docs/mo prefer template bundle at higher price; no evidence

regulatory_or_platform_dependency: Audit-trail/legal admissibility expectations; state lease law varies
major_uncertainty: Saturated, free tiers; no demand evidence gathered

dimension_reasons.competition_gap: Free tiers from SignWell and others
dimension_reasons.regulatory_simplicity: ESIGN broadly permissive but state lease law varies

verdict_reason: Saturated with free incumbents; only 2 evidence items obtained (research limit reached)

name: Webhook capture and replay for small teams
buyer: Indie devs/small teams consuming Stripe/GitHub/Shopify webhooks
pain: Hard to reproduce events, replay with valid signatures, missed events

evidence.shows: Developer $0 (10k events, 3-day retention); Team from $39/mo (7 days); Growth from $499/mo (fact)
Describes replay/re-sign pain: re-triggering events is the bottleneck; signature fail on replay (fact; vendor marketing)
Another webhook-inspect/replay tool launched with 0 upvotes (fact); shows crowding and weak traction
Stripe retries up to 3 days live; Dashboard resend 15 days, CLI resend 30 days; stripe listen for local testing (fact)

entrant_edge.entrant_basis: Hookdeck free tier is $0; no edge
entrant_edge.falsifier: Pay signal at $9 in a niche Hookdeck free tier does not serve

regulatory_or_platform_dependency: Own infra; no platform lock besides provider webhooks
major_uncertainty: Free incumbent tiers and provider-native tools

dimension_reasons.competition_gap: Hookdeck free tier, Stripe CLI, webhook.site, clones

verdict_reason: Free incumbent tiers plus provider-native tools; no entrant edge
unknowns: Hookdeck per-event rates inconsistent on page

name: Normalized SEC XBRL financials API for indie quant/AI builders
buyer: Indie devs/students/small fintech startups needing clean US-company fundamentals
pain: Raw EDGAR XBRL needs heavy normalization

evidence.shows: Free 100 calls; Personal/Startups $49/mo; Business $199/mo; extra data $0.30/GB (fact)
EDGAR submissions/XBRL APIs and nightly bulk ZIPs are free, no API key; SEC gives no technical support (fact)
Existence of paid tiers incl. startup plan suggests paying behavior for wrappers around free data (inference, no customer counts)

entrant_wedge: Pre-normalized fundamentals (standardized line items) over free SEC bulk data; niche pricing

entrant_edge.entrant_basis: No demonstrable edge versus established wrapper; value would be modeled
entrant_edge.falsifier: If no buyer pays >$20/mo for normalized fundamentals in a trial landing test, reject

unit_economics.notes: Model: public data bulk download, hosting small; SEC fair-access rate limit not verified (fetch failed)

regulatory_or_platform_dependency: SEC fair-access/terms (rate limit unverified); XBRL data quality
major_uncertainty: Entrant has no moat vs sec-api.io; normalization correctness

dimension_reasons.competition_gap: Established paid wrapper but gap in niche normalization unproven
dimension_reasons.platform_resilience: Public gov data, no platform ban

verdict_reason: Free public data with low cost; keep for deep dive to test demand, though no proven edge

name: Hosted MCP server generator for SaaS APIs
buyer: Small API/SaaS vendors wanting MCP exposure
pain: Need an MCP server without building one

evidence.shows: Only Enterprise tier shown with 'custom server creation' for MCP; no public prices (fact)
Free plan $0 up to 5 generators (SDK/docs/MCP server); other tiers not priced on page (fact)
Official MCP Registry exists, so discovery channel is open; server count not obtainable (fact)

entrant_wedge: Self-serve low-price hosted MCP for small API vendors

entrant_edge.entrant_basis: Free tier exists at Stainless; entrant not cheaper
entrant_edge.falsifier: No small vendor pays for hosted MCP in landing test

major_uncertainty: Whether demand is paying vs free; incumbents backed by funding

dimension_reasons.competition_gap: Free generator exists; mid-market self-serve gap unverified

verdict_reason: Possible mid-market gap (incumbent prices opaque); worth deep dive but demand unproven
